  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are not
listed on the agenda but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action may be
taken, the Commission and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing response. Each
speaker is limited to (3) three minutes. Time may be surrendered by deferring (1) one minute to another speaker,
not to exceed a total of (8) eight minutes. The speaker wishing to defer time must be present when the item is
heard. In order to be recognized and present an item, each speaker must complete and submit to the Recording
Secretary a Request to Speak form prior to the beginning of the item being announced by the Chair (forms are
available at the entrance to the meeting room). Speakers are taken in the order slips are submitted.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous meeting
where the public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not subject to public
 Public Works Commission  Page 3 of 3  March 26, 2025

discussion at this meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final. Resolutions concerning
decisions made at previous meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the decision to assure the accuracy of
the findings, the prior vote, and any conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If discussion is
desired, an item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration. Commissioners may
indicate a negative or abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to the vote on the motion to
adopt the entire Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission
following the action on the Consent Calendar. The Commission first will take up the items for which public
speaker requests have been submitted. Public speakers shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral
Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this meeting
with no final action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral
Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment shall
follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above are
on file in the Public Works Department, Malibu City Hall, 23825 Stuart Ranch Road, Malibu, California and are
available for public inspection during regular office hours which are 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Monday through
Thursday, and 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Friday. Written materials distributed to the Commission within 72 hours
of the Commission meeting are available for public inspection immediately upon distribution (Government Code
Section 54957.5(b)(2). Copies of staff reports and written materials may be purchased for $0.10 per page.
Pursuant to State law, this agenda was posted at least 72 hours prior to the meeting.

The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for the
deaf (TDD), please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In compliance
with the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please
contact Environmental Sustainability Director Yolanda Bundy, (310) 456-2489, ext. 229. Notification 48 hours
prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting.
[28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II].

Requests for use of audio or video equipment during a Commission meeting should be directed to the Media Team
at (310) 456-2489, ext. 227, or media@malibucity.org. Materials must be submitted by 12:00 p.m. on the day of
the meeting.

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California, that the foregoing agenda was
posted in accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Dated this 20th day of March 2025.

Subject:  Capital Improvement Projects and Disaster Recovery Projects Status
  Report

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file report on the status of the City’s current and
upcoming Capital Improvement Projects and Disaster Recovery Projects.

DISCUSSION: One of the responsibilities of the Public Works Department is to manage
the design and construction of Capital Improvement Projects (CIP). CIPs are the backbone
of the community. These projects are essential for maintaining and enhancing the City's
infrastructure, ensuring public safety, and improving the overall quality of life for the
residents. CIPs not only address immediate needs but also lay groundwork for future
resilience against natural disasters.

 The following are some project highlights:

Permanent Skate Park
This project plans and specifications are finalized and will be advertised for construction
bids on December 12, 2024. Construction bids were received on January 30, 2025, and
the City received three construction bids. On March 10, 2025, the City Council awarded
the project to the low bidder. Construction is estimated to start in the Spring 2025.

Civic Center Water Treatment Facility Phase 2
The project design was finalized in 2022 and was being reviewed by the State Water Board
for approval. The project is to be financed through a low interest state loan program by the
State Water Board. During the review process, a significant cultural resource discovery
was found. Due to this discovery, the City and Regional Board have revised the project
boundaries to eliminate the section where the cultural resources were discovered. The
revised MOU was scheduled to be presented to the LA Regional Board for adoption.
However, the Franklin and Palisades Fires have put this revision on hold. Staff is meeting
with the Regional Boad to develop a revised plan.

Bluffs Park Snack Shack
This project include the construction of a prefabricated building for a snack shack, storage
and restrooms. A design consultant agreement was approved by the City Council at the
meeting on November 25, 2025, meeting. Staff is currently scheduling a project kick off
meeting and will be developing a project schedule.

PCH Signal Synchronization System Improvements Project
Project construction for the PCH Signal Synchronization System Improvements Project is
proceeding with the construction. The contractor is continuing to install the traffic signal
improvements associated with this project. It is anticipated that this project will be
completed by the Summer of 2025.

PCH Roundabouts at El Matador State Beach and Encinal Canyon Road
The City and Caltrans was approached by the County regarding the construction of two
roundabouts on PCH. The County has additional Metro funding available and was seeking
to apply this funding towards a PCH safety project. The 2015 PCH Safety Study and the
Caltrans’ Road Safety Audits have identified a roundabout at these two locations. The
County will be transferring their Metro funds to the City to facilitate the design and
construction of the roundabout. The project scope of work includes constructing two
roundabouts utilizing easy to install, modular roundabout systems from recycled materials.
Project funding was approved by Metro in February and the project is anticipated to be
completed by Fall 2025.

PCH Speed Enforcement Cameras
On September 27, 2024, the Governor signed SB 1297 authorizing speed enforcement
cameras to be installed in Malibu to protect public safety on PCH. The new law allows the
placement of cameras in five locations on PCH – Decker Canyon Road, between
  Page 2 of 3
  Agenda Item # 4.A.
 Guernsey Avenue and Morning View Drive, Latigo Canyon Road, Carbon Canyon Road,
Tuna Canyon Road. These new enforcement cameras also require the installation of new
speed feedback signs. The new camera poles and speed feedback signs will require a
CDP. Staff is currently working on this application. Once this is completed, the project
(poles and speed feedback signs) will be advertised for construction. Staff is also working
on a Speed Enforcement Camera Use Policy and Impact Report. Once this report is
completed, staff will proceed with procuring and installing the speed enforcement
cameras. The goal is to have full implementation by November 2025.

Franklin and Palisades Fire Guardrail Replacement
This project is an emergency contract as the result of the Franklin and Palisades fires and
includes the replacement of the metal beam guardrails within these two fire perimeters.
The emergency contractor has secured the required materials and will begin this project
during the week of March 24, 2025.

Palisades Fire Big Rock Storm Drain Repairs
This project includes the replacement of over 6,000 linear feet of storm drains within the
Big Rock neighborhood. The project will also repair or replace any below ground catch
basins which may have been damaged from the fires. Two emergency contractors have
been hired to complete the repairs. The construction materials have been ordered and
delivered. The work is likely to start during the week of March 17, 2025.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Review and provide input on the proposed Capital
Improvement Projects for Fiscal Year 2025-2026.

DISCUSSION: Each year the Public Works Department prepares a list of Capital
Improvement Projects for the upcoming fiscal year as part of the budget process. These
projects are discussed with the Public Works Commission (Commission) and the
Commission will provide a recommendation. During the preparation of the Fiscal Year
2025-2026 budget, some of these projects may be removed and other projects may be
added. Below is a list of projects that are proposed to be included in the Fiscal Year 2025-
2026 Budget.

Current projects to be incorporated in FY26 Budget

their complexity. They typically start in a specific budget year and extend to two or more
years. These projects are typically extended into the following budget year. The following

Proposed Projects
The following are a list of new projects being proposed to the Fiscal Year 2025-2026
Budget. Some of these projects were developed from the City’s long term 5-Year CIP and
others were requested from other City departments.

Point Dume Storm Drain Improvements, Phase 1
This project consists of performing street resurfacing throughout Heathercliff Road,
Wandermere Road, Grayfox Street, Boniface Drive, Portshead Road, Selfridge Drive and
Wildlife Road.

Malibu Bluffs Park Prefabricated Score Sheds
The project will consist of installing prefabricated sheds to store the scoreboards used by
Malibu Little League.

Malibu Bluffs Park Parking Lot Resurfacing
This project will consist of resurfacing the parking lot at Malibu Bluffs Park located at 24250
Pacific Coast Highway.

Malibu Bluffs Park Workout Station Repairs
The project consists of removing and installing new workout stations at Malibu Bluffs Park.
The previously installed workout stations have completed their lifecycle.

Malibu Bluffs Park Little League Irrigation Improvements
This project will include improving the irrigation at Malibu Bluffs Park.

Las Flores Creek Park Repairs
Las Flores Creek Park was damaged by the Palisades Fire. Repairs include replacing the
advanced onsite water treatment system, the playground structures, the trails, irrigation
and replacing the landscaping.

Land Management System

  Page 2 of 3
  Agenda Item # 4.B.
 The new land management system or “permitting software” system, is intended to be
brought for Council’s consideration and approval with kick-off during the upcoming
calendar year and will promote resiliency and improve permit processing timelines.

City Hall Carpet Replacement
The project will consist of removing and replacing the carpet in City Hall for both the
upstairs and downstairs areas. The existing carpet in City Hall has reached its lifecycle.

City Hall HVAC Repairs
The project will consist of repairing the HVAC system in City Hall

Harvest Road Storm Drain Improvements
This project consists of constructing new inlet/outlet headwalls and removing and
replacing 50 linear feet of 30-inch RCP pipe located on Harvester Road.

Grayfox and Fernhill Sidewalk Repairs
This project consists of repairing the damaged walkways on Grayfox Street and Fernhill
Drive that have been damaged from tree roots. These repairs will eliminate tripping
hazards by removing the existing street trees.

Malibu Park Storm Drain Improvements
This project will include replacing the existing metal storm drain pipes with concrete storm
drain pipes. The project will also conduct repairs to catch basins and other storm drainage
facilities within the Malibu Park neighborhood.

Point Dume Resurfacing Project
This project includes resurfacing Wandermere from Heathercliff Road to the end,
Portshead Road from PCH to Boniface Drive, Selfridge Drive from Portshead Road to
Wildlife Road, Boniface Drive from Portshead Road to Fernhill Drive, Wildlife Road from
Zumirez Drive to Fernhill Drive, and Grayfox Street from Dume Drive to Fernhill Drive.

Civic Center Way Sidewalk Repairs
This project consists of repairing approximately 300 linear feel of sidewalk damaged by a
series of storms over the recent years.

Staff is seeking additional comments or project suggestions to the Proposed Capital
Improvement Projects list for Fiscal Year 2025-2026.

DISCUSSION: At the June 24, 2024, Regular Council meeting, the Council approved a
list of assignments for Fiscal Year 2024-2025 for the Public Works Commission
(Attachment 1). The Commission assignments included the requirement for each
Commission to provide the City Council with a mid-year written report of Commission
activities.

The Commission is requested to develop a list of its activities and recommendations made
to the City Council during the first half of the fiscal year (July through December 2024).
The City Manager will present mid-year reports from all the Commissions to the City
Council in February 2024. The Commission Chair is requested to attend the meeting to
answer any questions the Councilmembers may have.

A draft memorandum listing Commission actions (Attachment 2) has been prepared by
staff for Commission review, and additional items may be added, if necessary

  City of Malibu
  MEMORANDUM

To:  Public Works Commission

From:  Steve McClary, City Manager

Date:  June 26, 2024

Re:  Public Works Assignments for Fiscal Year 2024-25

At its Regular meeting on June 24, 2024, the City Council approved assignments for the Public Works
Commission during Fiscal Year 2024-2025:

  1.  Review and make recommendations to the City Council on Capital Improvement and Disaster
  Projects

  2.  Review and make recommendations to the City Council for an updated five-year Capital
  Improvement Projects Plan

  3.  Report on the status of Los Angeles County Waterworks, District 29 infrastructure and make
  recommendations toward long-term solutions

  4.  Review utility undergrounding options within the City

  5.  Review parking issues citywide

  6.  Review and make recommendations regarding a Green Fleet Policy

  7.  Review and make recommendations regarding a Neighborhood Beautification Program

  8.  Review the maintenance and monitoring of the City’s landslide assessment districts

  9.  Review and make recommendations on the Pavement Management Plan

  10.  Review the operation and maintenance of the wastewater and stormwater treatment facilities

  11.  Review and make recommendations on offsite Private Development mitigation measures that
  are constructed within the public right-of-way

  12.  Incorporate discussion of alternative transportation modes, such as bike lanes, in all road
  improvement projects

  13.  Make bimonthly oral reports to the City Council on Commission activity

  14.  Submit a mid-year written report to the City Council on Commission activities
